articleTitle: Sustainable Energy Generation using Animate Prime Movers – A Research Note on Methodology, Simulation and AI system training
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: As the United Nations stresses towards clean energy, via its sustainable development goals (goal number 7), animate prime movers are yet another renewable energy resource, which may contribute towards the betterment of humanity. Though considered out-of-place in the modern and futuristic human society, their appropriate utilization, while ensuring welfare elements, can still provide benefits to mankind. In fact, various modern pieces of research mention animal based work in different areas. The current article discusses two concept schemes for renewable/sustainable power generation via animals – issues with prior art have been discussed to bring out the effectiveness of the presented schemes. Furthermore, a simulation based study has been presented in this article, which is another contribution, because studies of animal based power generation, generally do not include simulation work. Lastly, a methodology for training an expert system to detect the fatigue of a power generating animal, has also been briefly discussed in this manuscript.

articleTitle: Monitoring Magnetic Flux Density of 100 KVA Transformer Operational Remotely
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Transformers are important equipment in transmission and distribution networks. Its operation and control are important aspects which determine the reliability and quality of power supply. As many stepdown transformers are spread over a wide area in the present power system, it is difficult to monitor the condition of each transformer manually. Therefore, development of a Condition Monitoring System (CMS) for transformers is performed. This condition monitoring system can monitor several parameter values of a transformer in real time. This paper presents the design of a sensing system allowing measurement of magnetic flux and load parameter at the transformer. These parameters are current, voltage, temperature, magnetic flux density and total losses at any instant at a particular transformer. The sensors monitoring these parameters can be interfaced to master and slave microcontrollers working as an onboard computer at the transformer that can collect sensing data and send it to a hub monitoring the status of the transformers in power supply network to have continuous supply of power to consumers. The hub monitoring the transformer may be placed at the power distribution company and at the transformer manufacturer’s site to assess the performance of transformers statistically and take corrective action where it is necessary. The CMS is intended to be easily incorporated into the transformer configurations, requiring little modification of the existing infrastructure and easily manageable through recalibration and replacement of sensors every now and then. The system does, however, require initial installation costs, but these are offset by many advantages that include increased transformer lifespan, less operational time lost, and improved energy efficiency, with payback expected within 2-3 years.

articleTitle: VigilantAI: Real-time detection of anomalous activity from a video stream using deep learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: In an era where artificial intelligence (AI) solutions are increasingly integrated into various sectors, we have utilized Artificial Intelligence for enhancing public safety through real-time detection of illegal activities such as robberies and threats at gunpoint using CCTV footage. With the proliferation of deep learning in object detection, the study focuses on deploying the YoloV5 model, trained on a custom dataset compiled from diverse CCTV sources and movies, to identify specific criminal actions. One of the major problems faced in this field is the availability of a large robust labeled dataset on which a deep learning model can be trained. For this purpose, we have created our own dataset by converting various CCTV footage and movies into images, and then labeling them with the correct class. In addition, we also augmented data by using various data augmentation techniques for the chosen images. This dataset, enriched through augmentation techniques and annotated with bounding boxes, allows for the precise detection of threats, achieving an accuracy rate of 85%. Our system stands out by not only spotting these activities but also by instantly alerting security personnel, facilitating a rapid response to potentially dangerous situations. This capability is important for law enforcement agencies worldwide, offering them an advanced tool to act swiftly and prevent crimes, thereby enhancing public security. The essence of our work demonstrates the practical application and significant impact of AI in bolstering security measures, providing a solid foundation for future enhancements in the field. Through this initiative, we aim to foster a safer environment in public spaces, reducing crime rates and increasing the general public’s sense of safety.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Self-Sufficient Photovoltaic Park for Sustainable Energy Independence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Over time, energy needs grow as distant regions of countries transform into new cities and as electronic devices and electrical applications become more prevalent in daily life, resulting in massive energy demands. The current energy situation in Pakistan necessitates the effective use of renewable energy sources. The nation, having the most potential for solar energy, is seeing incredible advancements in the production of electricity from photovoltaic sources. Pakistan faces a severe financial and energy crisis due to currency collapse, making it difficult to invest in renewable energy sources. The Makran division, located 700 kilometers from Sindh and Balochistan, has the potential for solar energy production. However, Pakistan imports energy to meet domestic and industrial needs. Iran’s neighboring country produces excess electricity, which Pakistan imports. In 2023, transmission line malfunctions caused power outages in the Makran division, affecting daily activities. The 200 MW Grid Connected Photovoltaic Power Park (GCPPP) in the Makran division produces clean, green energy, eliminating the need to pay additional fees to neighboring nations. The GCPPP has a performance ratio of 84.2% and, the GCPPP records 1958.9 kWh/m2 of direct global horizontal irradiation and 884.3 kWh/m2 of diffuse horizontal irradiation on the solar cell surface. It is expected to benefit Pakistan in future installations, especially in remote locations.

articleTitle: Assessing the Integration of Solar Power Generation within the CASA-1000 HVDC Transnational Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Transnationally linked renewable power generation systems contribute significantly to reducing global warming and decarbonizing the energy sector. High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmission lines are preferred over High Voltage Alternating Current (HVAC) systems due to their lower power losses. Solar power generation, in particular, is becoming increasingly popular due to its direct current (DC) nature, which makes it more economical for long-distance transmission via HVDC lines. Central Asian nations, especially Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan, have substantial potential for hydro and solar power generation. Utilizing an HVDC network to minimize line losses, these renewable energy resources can be exported to South Asian countries like Afghanistan and Pakistan, which are currently facing multiple energy crises. This research primarily focuses on estimating solar power generation potential in Central Asian countries where the HVDC converter stations of the CASA-1000 project are available. As the electricity demand in these Central Asian countries rises in the future, the power generated from the proposed solar power plants will be transmitted through the HVDC network. Currently, excess power generated by hydro power plants in these countries during the summer can be complemented by solar power plants in the winter, ensuring a consistent power supply. The proposed design includes three solar power plants: a 650 MWp DC plant in Khujand, a 240 MWp DC plant in Sangtuda, Republic of Tajikistan, and a 632.5 MWp DC plant in Datka, Kyrgyzstan. These plants will help maintain electricity continuity throughout the winter and beyond, as the demand for electricity in Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan increases. With performance ratios exceeding 87%, as determined by PVSyst software, and efficient transmission via the CASA-1000 HVDC network, this design is both cost-effective and environmentally friendly, providing clean and green electricity to South Asian nations. Integrating photovoltaic-based power plants into the existing plan will ensure year-round power continuity.

articleTitle: Identification and Classification of Fingerprints Using Automated Deep-Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Fingerprint Identification Systems (AFIS) face significant challenges in real-time applications due to the vast number of comparisons required for large fingerprint databases. To address this, we present a deep learning-based fingerprint categorization technique to enhance individual identification efficiency. To address This categorization technique uses deep learning to find specific fingerprint information. Specific fingerprint information, including left-right hand classification, sweat-pore classification, scratch classification, and finger classification, was intended to be distinguished by the suggested method. The fingerprint dataset Scoring was collected from a public fingerprint dataset. The proposed CNN model, implemented in Python and Google Colab, enhances biometric systems effectiveness by using deep learning techniques like Resnet 50, MobileNet, LeNet, and Hybrid model, demonstrating its strengths. The results of the planned research would be helpful for business and for assisting investigators in connecting one crime scene to another involving the same suspect.

articleTitle: Meta-Learning for Automated Algorithm Selection in Healthcare: Enhancing Clinical Outcomes through Data-Driven Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: The integration of machine learning (ML) algorithms in healthcare is transforming diagnostics, treatment planning, and patient management. However, the complexity and diversity of these algorithms, coupled with heterogeneous medical data, challenge practitioners without ML expertise. Traditional trial-and-error algorithm selection is inefficient and often suboptimal. This paper introduces a meta-learning framework for automated algorithm recommendation in medical applications. We extract a rich set of meta-features from 80 healthcare datasets, including statistical, information-theoretic, structural, landmarking, and complexity metrics. These meta-features train a Ridge regression meta-learner to model relationships between meta-features and the performance of eight classification algorithms. For any new healthcare task, the meta-learner predicts the most suitable algorithm based on the dataset’s meta-features. Our framework, evaluated on diverse real-world medical datasets, outperforms three other meta-learning systems in algorithm selection. By automating this process, we aim to enhance access to advanced ML, streamline workflows, and accelerate ML research translation into clinical practice, ultimately improving patient care and outcomes.

articleTitle: Traffic Sign Recognition System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Traffic Sign Recognition Systems (TSRS) are instrumental in improving road safety by assisting drivers and supporting autonomous vehicles in real-time identification of road regulations. These systems have advanced significantly in recent years, with deep learning approaches achieving promising results. However, despite these developments, existing models face challenges in adapting to the diverse conditions of real-world environments, including variations in lighting, weather, and sign appearance. Addressing this limitation, our study focuses on enhancing the robustness and accuracy of TSRS for practical deployment. In response to this gap, we introduce a novel deep learning model optimized for traffic sign recognition across various conditions. Our approach utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, which was trained on the German Traffic Sign Recognition (GTSR) dataset. We improved the model’s adaptability to new and unseen data while achieving a high accuracy rate of 97.99% by applying techniques like data augmentation and transfer learning. Methodologically, the model workflow includes extensive preprocessing, hyperparameter tuning, and real-time inference evaluations, ensuring suitability for deployment in autonomous driving systems. Our study contributes by providing a scalable, high-accuracy TSRS model that can reliably identify traffic signs in complex environments, supporting both autonomous and assisted driving technologies. The model’s performance paves the way for safer and more efficient road transport, while our results highlight the potential for further interdisciplinary research to expand TSRS capabilities.

articleTitle: Image Compression via Alternating Least Squares
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: In numerous application areas such as medical imaging and remote sensing, image compression methods play an important role in managing data storage and transmission costs. In this paper, we present an empirical study on a low-rank approximation using the alternating least squares (ALS) method for image compression. For high-dimensional data, we demonstrate the advantage of a matrix decomposition-based implementation that avoids explicit matrix inversion applied in the direct implementation in terms of computational efficiency. The performance of the ALS method is compared with the singular value decomposition in terms of information loss, and compression ratio.

articleTitle: Automatic Question Generation for Cognitive Domain of Outcome-Based Education System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: In recent years, the educational system has seen numerous improvements, including the addition of assessment criteria to evaluate educational outcomes. However, the manual creation of test questions often fails to accurately assess students’ competency levels and is time-consuming. This paper addresses the need for automated question generation (AQG) in the context of outcome-based education (OBE), a student-centric approach that has yet to incorporate AQG techniques. OBE, grounded in Bloom’s taxonomy, encompasses three domains: cognitive, psychomotor, and affective. Research focuses on the cognitive domain and its six levels of question generation. OBE algorithms for AQG are based on accuracy, time consumption, and question quality. The DistilBERT question-answering model and transformers for error correction are used in our AQG model. The model is trained on QGSTEC and assessed using performance measures. Comparatively, the model has higher accuracy, precision, and F1-score.

articleTitle: Innovative V2G System for Energy Management: Insights from MATLAB Simulink Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: The work presents a case study of the vehicle-to-grid (V2G) system which targets using electric vehicles (EVs) as a backup for energy management. It allows the transfer of surplus energy from EVs to the grid/ or for domestic use. This study considers a dual active bridge converter (DAB) for power control, an LCL filter for harmonic suppression, a phase lock loop (PLL) for synchronization to the grid, and an energy management system (EMS) for decision-making regarding energy sharing. In this study, a 53kW Tesla Roadstar battery is considered which is being charged by PV panels and used as a backup in peak hours when the EV is not in use. V2G is a complex system that consists of several sub-system designs. A complete design and selection criteria for these sub-systems are demonstrated through rigorous simulations using MATLAB Simulink. The results demonstrate the system’s capability to manage energy flows and maintain grid stability. Moreover, the charging of EVs through PV further contributes to green energy and relieves the stress on the conventional grid in peak hours.

articleTitle: Using Convolutional Neural Networks for Enhanced Pneumonia Detection via Chest X-Rays
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: As a deadly lung disease, pneumonia remains a leading cause of child mortality under five years old. Machine learning, especially deep learning have played a significant role in the improved performance for detection and identification of various diseases in the field of healthcare. Neural networks, especially the recent development of newer architectures, have revolutionized the object identification, and classification applications in clinical diagnosis of various diseases. This study presents the application of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for the timely and accurate detection of pneumonia using chest X-rays, a development with considerable potential in aiding clinical diagnosis. The research deployed dropout regularization in model design to mitigate overfitting and relied on recall and F1 scores for thorough model evaluation. Although comparable studies achieved higher overall accuracy, our models registered a recall rate of 98%, crucial in reducing false negatives and enhancing patient safety. This suggests the potential of our CNN model as a vital tool for healthcare professionals in early pneumonia detection in children and adults, with the capacity to process a high volume of X-ray images rapidly and accurately. The successful model construction was enabled through various parameter tuning techniques, thus enhancing patient care efficiency and the potential to decrease mortality rates.

articleTitle: An Ensemble Classification Approach for Efficient Disease Prediction in IoMT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: All over the world, chronic disease is one of the most common causes of death. To detect early disease, it is important to improve patient results. Early treatment can also significantly improve patient results. The main causes are drinking unclean water, an unhealthy diet, addiction, and many more to enroll the patient in chronic disease. The critical challenge is to analyze the data for early disease detection. In an IoMT setup, different sensors collect medical data and send it through different gateways to store it in the cloud. The main issue facing the healthcare industry is predicting the correct disease using data from medical devices in the form of sensors. The incomplete, noisy, inconsistent, error-prone data can compromise the performance of machine learning algorithms. Also, efficient prediction of machine learning models with greater accuracy is a prerequisite for such a setup so that medical practitioners can rely on the results, especially in cases where doctors are not available for physical examination. To address these limitations, we have proposed a methodology that pre-processes data and then applies ensemble techniques to predict the diseases. The comparison to the baselines indicates better performance in terms of performance metrics of Accuracy, Precision, and Recall.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Featured Based Standing Wheelchair Using Voice and Gesture Control for Enhancing Mobility and Accessibility
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: When it comes to independence and flexibility, the key issue that most affects the elderly and handicapped people is their ability to live freely and independently engage in and access parts of life. This research investigates and reveals a few derides difficulties, including physically challenged people having difficulty moving and patients wasting energy while operating a manual electrical wheelchair. Meanwhile, the risk of injury is greatest while transitioning to bed. So, the goal of this innovation is to solve the issues of three people at once. This wheelchair can stand and recline, which helps with a range of physical and medical concerns such as tight muscles, pressure points that cause pressure sores, poor blood circulation, and dependency on external aid. Furthermore, this prototype standing wheelchair may be operated by voice control or a control system on a smartphone device. Its ability to change from sitting to standing to recline and to automatically stop when it encounters a barrier is its standout feature. Adjustments for standing and reclining can be made via linear actuators. In an emergency, the wheelchair user’s precise location will be updated via a GPS tracking device. The ultrasonic sensor system for obstacle avoidance and the battery alarm system for charging needs will immediately notify the user.

articleTitle: Design and Analog Implementation of Synchronization Controllers for Feedback Instruments’ Servo Trainer Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: This paper describes the detailed implementation of synchronization controllers using operational amplifiers for the servo trainer modules manufactured by Feedback Instruments Inc. The existing curriculum provided along with these trainer modules lacks discussion and implementation on synchronization of servo systems. Synchronization of dynamical systems is of great significance and finds many applications in a diversity of disciplines. This work is directed to upgrade the curriculum of servo trainer modules with synchronization controllers such as proportional, proportional-integral, and state feedback controllers. Various plants’ states are read from the sensors on-board the servo trainers and provided to the controllers, which are implemented externally on breadboards. The controllers generate actuating signals which are fed to the servo trainer plants through the on-board motor amplifiers, thereby closing the feedback loop around the servo plants. The efficacy of the controllers is tested by exciting the master servo trainer system and recording the resulting master and slave servo trainer system trajectories through ESPIAL data acquisition software. It is experimentally found that the slave servo system follows the master servo system. In this way, synchronization of the master and slave servo plants is achieved. The proposed study will be a useful addition to the laboratory curriculum of linear control systems.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approaches for Extremism Detection: Challenges, Pitfall and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Social networks, such as Facebook, Twitter, and YouTube, are free for everyone, including extremist groups. These extremist groups may use social media to spread radical ideas, disseminate propaganda, and recruit young people to promote their cause. Therefore, identifying and eradicating extremist content is among the top challenges for technology companies, counter-terrorism agencies and regulatory authorities. In this study, we have reviewed extremism detection in social media literature. In particular, a systematic literature review is conducted and a synthesis of the literature is performed to examine the strengths and weaknesses of the existing studies on extremism detection. Furthermore, the challenges are identified and opportunities for future research are discussed. We contend that the results of the study can be used by researchers for a better comprehension of the landscape of online extremism extension, as well as to open new horizons for the research community.

articleTitle: Landslide Susceptibility Mapping for Muzaffarabad Region Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: In this study machine learning methods are proposed to identify landslides using data obtained from northern Pakistan (Muzaffarabad district). We used Random Forest, Decision Tree, gradient boosting machine (GBM), light gradient boosting machine (LGBM), neural network (NN), 1D-CNN (convolutional neural network one dimensional), XGBboost and Catboost for classification. Landslide is predicted with the dataset of 12 different factors and data of 1213 sites. First, we trained models individually and observed which one has the highest accuracy. Finally, the performances of applied models are assessed by using several statistical methods. Based on the results we obtained the highest accuracy is 85% of CNN and above 80% for boosting methods. The developed system can be effectively used to predict landslides of regions with similar environmental conditions.

articleTitle: A Framework for Vehicle and License Plate Detection in Pakistani Traffic Environments Using Algorithms Pool
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Automation of vehicle and license plate detection plays a vital role in several applications, such as security, traffic management, vehicle monitoring, tool collection, and parking-lot entry/exit control. This paper presents a framework to detect vehicles and license plates for Pakistani traffic environments. To detect vehicles and license plates, the proposed framework uses two pools to locate vehicles and license plates. Each of the pools uses two algorithms to locate vehicles and license plates. The pool of vehicle detection uses the Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) along with the Faster-RCNN. While the license plate detection pool uses an image processing-based technique along with the HSV segmentation method. Detailed simulations have been performed on our own collected 1142 diverse Pakistani traffic images. Our system achieves a mean accuracy of 90.26% and consumes less than 2 seconds on average to locate vehicles and license plates.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Leaf Classification for Agricultural Sustainability and Plant Species Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Agricultural production is critical for economic stability and food security, consequently early disease identification is essential for preserving plant health. Our study solves this need by incorporating Random Forest into a complete framework for leaf categorization. We recommend applying Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to construct an AI-driven, four-step procedure for this type of segregation. Crop images may be processed by preprocessing, segmenting, extracting features, and classifying them with Random Forest. During pre-processing, a Median Filter was applied, proceeded by thresholding for segmentation, eventually Kaze and HOG (Histogram of Oriented Gradient) were used to extract relevant features. A Random Forest classifier that has been optimized with PSO was used for classification. The random forest-based technique outperformed alternative methods such as naive-bayes and adaboost with an accuracy of 92.63

articleTitle: Identifying Authentic Reviews on Amazon Dataset using Transformer-Based Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Reviews and ratings significantly impact businesses, either boosting their reputation or harming competitors. To manipulate these outcomes, some businesses falsify product reviews. This paper introduces a transformer-based model that utilizes GloVe (Global Vectors for Word Representation) semantic embeddings to detect fraudulent reviews. Our approach captures subtle linguistic patterns indicative of fake reviews by fine-tuning a pre-trained GloVe model on a labelled dataset. The GloVe embeddings improve the model’s grasp of word semantics, while an attention-based neural network classifies reviews as genuine or fraudulent. Our model has surpassed traditional machine learning methods, achieving 98% accuracy across various datasets.

articleTitle: Knowledge Transfer In Cross Domain Recommender Systems Using Deep Latent Embeddings
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Traditional recommender systems often face challenges such as the cold-start problem and data sparsity, especially in cross-domain scenarios. These issues limit their ability to provide accurate recommendations for new users or items with minimal interaction data, reducing their effectiveness of personalized applications. To address these challenges, a novel approach is proposed leveraging knowledge transfer in cross-domain recommender systems using Deep Latent Embeddings. The proposed method uses an autoencoder-decoder architecture to learn latent representations of users and items in a source domain and transfers to a target domain with sparse data. By mapping data from both domains into a shared latent space, the proposed approach facilitates effective knowledge sharing, enabling personalized recommendations even in data-limited domains. The proposed system is evaluated on three real-world datasets from Amazon benchmark datasets i.e. Books, Digital Music, and Movies & TV, under three cross-domain scenarios: (1) Books to Digital Music, (2) Movies to Digital Music, and (3) Books to Movies & TV. Empirical results demonstrate significant improvements in recommendation quality, mitigating cold-start and data sparsity issues. This research advances cross-domain recommender systems, providing practical solutions to enhance user satisfaction and engagement in recommendation applications.

articleTitle: CFD Simulation for Monitoring and Ensuring Optimal Performance of Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Electricity has become an important part of the lives of modern people because of its need in the domestic and the industrial services. Due to the different ratings of electricity required in the different regions it becomes mandatory to maintain the electricity by stepping up or stepping down it with the aid of transformers. Ensuring the proper and safe usage of transformers, especially in remote areas, is a monumental and challenging task requiring meticulous attention to detail, comprehensive maintenance, thorough inspections, and adherence to safety protocols, with the difficulties further amplified by limited access to resources and specialized personnel. This study revolves around monitoring the flow characteristics of the transformer coolant fluid. Flow variables which include temperature, velocity and pressure are affected by load variations. The aim of this study is to ensure that there is continuous power supply as a part of a larger study that incorporates thousands of transformers operating at different locations. Monitoring of these transformers is done through connecting each transformer to data hubs at manufacturer site and power distribution company site by displaying the Augmented Reality of each transformer with real time support data statistically.

articleTitle: Efficient Smart Aeroponic Cultivation and Monitoring System Through Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: A cutting-edge method for growing plants without soil and with little water called aeroponics. The system is made up of two chambers within a structure; the plant with its stem and leaves will be in the top room, and the plant’s root will be exposed to a mist created by the nutritional solution in the bottom chamber. A Raspberry Pi will be the central controller for this system; it will automate operations and record various factors including humidity, pH, and temperature. Grow lights will be used to provide energy to the plant in place of the sun. The user will be able to monitor the system via an Android app that is interfaced with the microcontroller This will allow the application to receive real-time data and alert the user when any of the parameters are no longer appropriate for the plant. Additionally, the user has control over the mist, timing, and misters

articleTitle: Machine learning based fraudulent detection system for financial transactions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Maintaining the integrity of financial systems and preventing people and organizations from suffering financial losses depend heavily on the ability to spot fraudulent financial transactions. Traditional rule-based fraud detection methods have trouble identifying intricate patterns and developing fraud tactics. Machine learning approaches have become powerful fraud detection tools in recent years, utilizing the strength of data-driven models to spot fraudulent actions. The Existing rule-based fraud detection has difficulty in identifying complex patterns and evolving fraud tactics. This study thoroughly investigates the use of machine learning techniques, including decision trees and random forests, for financial transaction fraud detection, while also exploring feature engineering approaches to extract essential data from transaction records such as temporal, spatial, and relational features. In this study, real-world financial transaction datasets are used to conduct experimental evaluations, comparing the performance of various machine learning models based on accuracy, precision, recall, and F1- score. The results indicate that certain algorithms outperform others, demonstrating promising and favorable outcomes for CatBoost algorithm. This significance of our study lies in showcasing the effectiveness of machine learning techniques, compared to traditional rule-based methods, for detecting fraud in financial transactions, leading to more promising outcomes and contributing to the integrity and security of financial systems.

articleTitle: Peer Tutoring and its Impact on Academic Achievements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Peer tutoring is gaining attention rapidly nowadays, providing a learning environment where students have the opportunity to learn and grow through collaboration and effective communication. This study focuses on the impact of peer tutoring by collecting data from different students as well as surveys and then analyzing the pre and post-tutoring assessments to determine the impact of peer tutoring. It employs statistical techniques to study the impact of peer tutoring on both tutee and tutor, their self-confidence, and the overall academic achievement gained through tutoring.

articleTitle: Sustainable Photovoltaic System Integration for Urban Transit
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: As time goes on and demand for power rises daily, fossil fuels and conventional electricity sources become less and less viable. Developing countries such as Pakistan have the option to import gas and oil to generate energy in order to deal with a power deficit. Solar power generation is one of the most widely available and reasonably priced forms of renewable energy in the world. The technique employed to capture the available energy and the surrounding conditions have an impact on the performance of photovoltaic (PV) cells. Due to its solar band position at 33.9978°N latitude, 71.4887°E longitude, and elevation of 373 m, the proposed location in Pakistan’s Peshawar BRT Project that receives an average of 310 days of sunshine annually. PVSyst software is used to build and estimate the JinkoSolar 410Wp, 36V, 6874 kW Inverter Sungrow solar model cell performance research for an 80 MWp DC into 68.74 MWp AC load, for the suggested geographical location. Both the energy input into the grid and the different losses that occur within the system are examined; PV array selection and other parameters are also chosen for the proposed research; and the method of using an adjustable tilt angle to reduce losses has been put into practice. This study will help with the planning and forecasting of solar energy production for the same photovoltaic system on rooftops of other city metro stations, and it will make it easy to exchange all of the neighboring PV system components in Pakistan.

articleTitle: Electrified Transportation in Smart Cities: Optimal Utilization of PV for Electrified Railways and EV Charging Station
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: The integration of renewable energy sources into the conventional power system is becoming increasingly important for the attainment of sustainable energy solutions. The requirement of such integration is crucial in metropolitan cities for the reduction of carbon emissions and electricity costs. Considering urban transportation as a major source of carbon emissions in metropolitan cities, this study explores the energy management scheme for optimal utilization of photovoltaic (PV) for electrified railways and electric vehicle (EV) charging stations. The energy management system (EMS) is designed to prioritize the use of PV power, employing the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) technique using the perturb and observe (P&O) algorithm. In cases of insufficient or unavailable PV power, the system seamlessly draws power from the AC grid through a voltage source converter (VSC) to maintain a stable power supply to the electrified metro railway and EV charging station. Conversely, when PV generation exceeds demand, the surplus energy is fed back into the AC grid. The proposed approach works effectively for the seamless management of PV and grid power for EV charging stations and electrified railways, significantly reducing carbon emissions. For validation of the scheme, simulations were performed in MATLAB/Simulink, and results have been included.

articleTitle: Reinforcing Cyber Digital Twins for Protecting Critical Information Infrastructure (CII): Opportunities and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Digital Twin is hallmark of industrial revolution through automation and digitization. Digital Twin is an emerging technology domain to virtually model a physical system in a holistic fashion for enhanced productivity, seamless integration and effective supply chain. Digital Twin is digital replica of a physical process, system, product and service. It offers virtual modeling environment for monitoring and predicting possible outcome through simulation and real-time input of data. It replicates physical system in virtual space to manage the system through out its life-cycle. Digital Twin has diversified applications across various industrial sectors. Digital Twin being emerging technology has its associated misconceptions, challenges and opportunities. cyberphysical system and Digital Twins are vulnerable to cyber threats of diversified nature and magnitude. Digital Twin delineates mechanism for ascertaining operational-effectiveness and cyberreadiness of the CII. Digital Twin effectively addresses cyber security requirements of CII through virtual modeling, attack simulation and anomaly detection. Prognostic nature of Digital Twins aids in detecting targeted cyber attacks beforehand. Besides, digital twins offers prolific solutions for secure design and implementation of CII. Digital Twin technology merits adoption for protecting CII by addressing its associated challenges.

articleTitle: Streamlining Attendance with Voice Recognition via Gaussian Mixture Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Voice recognition systems are crucial because they allow seamless human-computer interaction and improve accessibility for users of all abilities. The use of these technologies in hands-free control, language translation, virtual assistants, transcription services, and hands-free control is revolutionising how we engage with technology and enhancing convenience and productivity in general. Several attendance systems based on voice recognition exist, but we wanted to deploy an attendance system with a good graphical user interface specifically for students of GIK Institute. For this purpose, we wanted to make a user-friendly and accurate voice recognition system based and trained on self-provided data of ten students. This study introduces an AI-driven attendance system, which demonstrates high efficiency and accuracy in identifying students’ daily class attendance. To achieve this, the Gaussian Mixture Model approach was employed. The paper also delves into the utilization of libraries and methods, encompassing the training and validation of well-known machine learning models. Additionally, the system’s performance, its strengths, weaknesses and potential areas for improvement are also discussed in the study.

articleTitle: Improving Gemstone Identification Accuracy Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Accurate identification of gemstones is crucial in various fields, including gemology research, jewelry appraisal, and consumer protection, where authenticity verification is paramount to prevent fraud and ensure trust in the gem trade. Traditional methods of gemstone identification heavily depend on the subjective expertise of gemologists, which can lead to inconsistencies and is often time-consuming, particularly when dealing with rare or complex gemstones. This study presents the development of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model designed for the automated classification of gemstones. The model leverages advanced image preprocessing techniques, including resizing, data augmentation, and normalization, to enhance the robustness of the classification process. Trained on a meticulously curated dataset comprising images of 15 distinct gemstone types, the CNN model achieved a notable validation accuracy of 88%. These results highlight the potential of CNN-based approaches as a reliable and efficient alternative to traditional gemstone identification methods, offering significant improvements in speed, consistency, and scalability.

articleTitle: Vehicle Detection and Classification in Aerial Images with YOLOv8 and CNN-BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: The detection and classification of vehicles in complex traffic monitoring systems pose significant challenges that demand innovative solutions. Traditional methods often struggle with high computational requirements and the need to integrate diverse data sources. This research presents a strong framework particularly built for vehicle classification in aerial picture sequences. Our method comprises georeferencing, preprocessing, segmentation, and detection using the YOLOv8 algorithm, augmented by feature extraction utilizing BRIEF and FAST approaches. For the classification, we utilize a hybrid model that blends Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks, providing extensive analysis and assessment. By integrating these advanced methodologies, our framework significantly improves vehicle detection and classification, thereby enhancing traffic management and surveillance systems. Experimental results on the Vehicle Aerial Imagery from a Drone (VAID) dataset demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods, achieving an impressive accuracy of 0.93%. This demonstrates the efficiency of our method in recognizing and classifying cars in aerial imagery, representing a major advancement over past techniques.

articleTitle: Clinical Reports Classification using Fine-Tuned DistilBERT Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Due to the fast-growing nature of healthcare data, information extraction from clinical reports is becoming challenge. Because clinical reports are covering a major portion of patient care. These reports are unstructured and densely composed with specialized medical terminology which makes it quite difficult for efficient classification and retrieval. This study deploys a novel fine-tuned Transformer model, DistilBERT, to automatically classify clinical reports. Various preprocessing steps are conducted, to normalize the data and remove the redundant information. Various padding approaches are applied and hyperparameters are tuned to obtained better results. The proposed model is validated using the i2b2 dataset. The proposed model achieves the highest accuracy of 0.92%. The obtained results are better compared to state-of-the art works. This study provides a scalable and robust solution for classifying clinical reports, which contributes to the field of medical informatics by assisting in reducing the workload on health professionals due to manual triage based only on reading list table information.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Pregnancy Monitoring: Machine Learning for Trimester Classification Using Biomechanical Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: To ensure the health of both the mother and the growing fetus, pregnancy has to be closely monitored. However, traditional methods of monitoring pregnancy often focus on physiological and biochemical changes instead of biomechanical alterations. Plantar pressure and balance distribution are considered as indicators for monitoring pregnancies, but recent studies mainly involve manual techniques or unsophisticated statistical methods which may not fully capture the complex biomechanical changes that take place within a trimester period. Therefore, this study proposes a trimester-based classification model in pregnant women using various machine learning (ML) algorithms according to plantar pressure and balance distribution data so as to have specific essentials ranges through which gestation development can be monitored effectively. Advanced ML algorithms such as K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Random Forest (RF), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) are used in this research to measure subtle kinematics variations. Feature extraction from force plate data is able to capture vital aspects of plantar pressure and balance. First, second, and third trimester samples were employed for constructing the training set and testing the classification model by applying it on them respectively. The method’s aim is to improve prenatal care by giving a digital diagnosis of trimesters based on quantitative biomechanical data. This model aims to prove that machine learning can be implemented using biomechanical data with an accuracy rate up to 80 percent, particularly when KNN approach is used in order to fill the gap in current methods.

articleTitle: Thermal Monitoring of 100 KVA Transformer Operations at Remote Locations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Electricity has become an integral part of modern life and is equally used for domestic purposes and industrial services. The distribution of electricity utilizes transformers to either step down or step up the voltage levels depending on whether it is used for homes or industrial consumption. It is a monumental activity to maintain proper and safe usage of transformers, especially when dealing with remote areas. In this paper, the focus is on the significance of monitoring thermal parameters of transformers. It investigates the effect of load variations on transformer output. The aim of this study is to ensure that there is continuous power supply from thermal perspective, as a part of a larger study; that encompasses thousands of transformers operating at different rural and urban locations and also studies magnetism and fluid dynamics aspects.

articleTitle: Using Autoencoder as Feature Extractor for Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Malware detecting approaches suffer many limitations, and all anti-malware solutions have failed to be reliable enough for detecting zero day malware. Signature based solutions depend upon the signatures generated only when malware surfaces at least once in the cyber world. Another approach that works by detecting the anomalies caused in the environment can easily be defeated by diligently and intelligently written malware. Solutions trained to observe the behavior for detecting malicious files have failed to cater to the malware capable of detecting the sandboxed or protected environment. Machine learning and deep learning based approaches greatly suffer in training their models with either an imbalanced dataset or an inadequate number of samples. AI based anti-malware solutions that have been trained with enough samples targeted a selected feature vector thus ignoring the input of leftover features in the maliciousness of malware just to cope with the lack of underlying hardware’s processing power. Our research focuses on producing an anti-malware solution for detecting malicious PE files by circumventing the earlier mentioned shortcomings. Our proposed framework, which is based upon automated feature engineering through autoencoders, trains the model over a fairly large dataset. It focuses on the visual patterns of malware samples to automatically extract the meaningful part of the visual pattern. Our experiment has successfully produced a state-of-the-art accuracy of 99.54

articleTitle: ASL Recognition using Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: There is a considerably vast communication gap between deaf and hearing individuals, and one potential solution is the development of American Sign Language (ASL) recognition technology. While methods utilizing deep learning and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown promising results in general ASL recognition tasks, the potential of optimized CNN architectures for ASL recognition remains untapped. This research identifies the ideal CNN structure to achieve best ASL recognition in static images. The VGG16 model has come out to be very effective; however, analyzing multiple CNN implementations may provide interesting perspectives which could in turn expose features that could potentially be helpful in ASL recognition. This experiment compares the performance of a fine-tuned ResNet50 CNN model with a baseline VGG16 model in ASL recognition. Through analysis of each model’s respective strengths and weaknesses, the study aims to identify areas within the VGG16 architecture that may be further optimized to produce precise results. This research project provides guidance for picking suitable CNN architectures and offers valuable insights for improving VGG16 model to achieve even better accuracy and robust results.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Head Pose Estimation Algorithms for Sign Language Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Head pose estimation (HPE) can be used in sign language linguistics and gesture studies, particularly for quantitative assessment of head movements in terms of yaw, pitch, and roll. These measurements can be used to quantify and compare different types of head movements within and across sign languages and co-speech gesture. While optoelectronic camera-based motion capture systems are considered the gold standard for this purpose, their practicality is limited due to high costs, accessibility issues, and the need for markers on the signer’s face. Despite the popularity of HPE as a research area, there has been limited validation of HPE algorithms based on RGB videos, which is more suitable for sign language analysis, and almost no testing using sign-language specific data. This study addresses this gap by providing an overview of existing HPE algorithms and evaluating three state-of-the-art algorithms—MediaPipe, OpenFace, and 6DRepNet—using RGB sign language videos from a MoCap dataset of Finnish Sign Language. The accuracy of these algorithms is compared against an optoelectronic camera-based motion capture system recordings of the same data. The results indicate a good performance of all three algorithms for measuring yaw (with some advantages of MediaPipe), and worse performance for measuring pitch and roll.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approaches for Precision Agriculture: Weed and Cotton Crop Classification Using YOLO and Faster RCNN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Weed infestation in cotton fields significantly challenges agricultural productivity by competing for essential nutrients and water resources. This study presents a comprehensive comparative analysis of two deep learning-based object detection models - YOLO and Faster R-CNN - for automated weed detection in cotton fields. We developed and annotated a custom dataset comprising field images captured under various environmental conditions, labelled in both COCO and YOLO formats using Label Studio. Performance evaluation revealed the YOLO model’s superior capabilities, achieving a mAP50 of 0.775, precision scores of 0.859 for cotton and 0.656 for weed detection, and recall rates of 0.849 and 0.543 for cotton and weed respectively on the test dataset. In comparison, Faster R-CNN showed lower performance with AP scores of 0.708 for cotton and 0.269 for weed detection, particularly struggling with objects of varying sizes. The YOLO model maintained consistent performance across both validation and test datasets, with validation metrics showing mAP50 of 0.982 and mAP50-95 of 0.829. These results establish YOLO’s effectiveness as a reliable tool for automated weed detection in cotton fields, offering a practical solution for precision agriculture applications. The developed model demonstrates the potential for integration into automated crop management systems, contributing to more efficient and targeted weed control strategies.

articleTitle: Content Moderations without Labels: Unsupervised Classification of Hateful Texts
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: In today’s digital age, social media platforms serve as forums for diverse discussions. However, they also facilitate the spread of hate speech due to online anonymity and the lack of accountability. Islamophobia, a prevalent issue in this context, can have real-world consequences for Muslim communities. This study aims to assess how effectively we can classify social media text as Islamic and Islamophobic. Leveraging advanced natural language processing techniques, we explore the underlying topics in these discussions. Using Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and BERTopic as our topic models, we extract robust features from these posts to guide the classification process. A key aspect of our research involves the use of unsupervised text classification methods, enabling us to utilize vast amounts of unannotated social media data. For unsupervised text classification, we used Doc-SCAN and Lbl2Vec. We trained and evaluated these techniques on the two tasks of Islamic and Islamophobic Classification and on the two datasets of Twitter and Reddit posts. The combination of LDA as the topic model and Lbl2Vec as the classifier emerged as the most effective technique, consistently achieving the highest scores across all tasks and datasets. It yielded weighted average F1 scores of 89% on Reddit and 87% on Twitter for the Islamic classification task, and 82% on Twitter for the Islamophobic classification task.

articleTitle: Advanced Gait Event Recognition and Pose Estimation Model through Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Analyzing activities of humans, events, Gait, human-to-human interaction, and sports analysis are some prominent subjects, and key areas of interest in machine learning, artificial intelligence, and deep learning fields. Nevertheless, beginning with intelligent computing in a somewhat less complex context for enhanced scene perception remains a topic that still waits for scholars’ exploration. In this system, we have made a model to allow machines to understand the behaviors in the external environment by proposing a novel methodology to discern sports and events. This research aims to incorporate AI functions in information technologies to innovative future trajectories of intelligent media. Our proposed system recognizes complex human activities from two well-known Kinetics and YouTube datasets. After preprocessing and human detection, we have used numerous feature algorithms, such as DOF and 3D cartesian plane for joint points while distance transform and optical flow for full body points. These feature point values are then fed to joint feature descriptors and PSO for enhancement before passing to the CNN for recognition. However, the obtained data prove that the suggested approach is effective in realistic scenarios with a high level of uncertainty with an accuracy of 91.2% and 88.2%, on Kinetics and YouTube datasets respectively.

articleTitle: Enhancing Fake News Detection Using BERT: A Comparative Analysis of Logistic Regression, RFC, LSTM and BERT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: The research analyzed how to identify fake news effectively, understanding the developing capabilities to differentiate between misinformation and the correct nature of news in today’s complex media environment. Numerous approaches were tested: mostly the ways of determining if a certain message is valid or false. With application of Logistic Regression, Random Forest and lastly LSTM models, the research has been able to achieve 98.7%, 98.8%, and 95% accuracies respectively, showing that these traditional and advanced techniques are very effective. However, it became apparent that these models performed poorly as soon as tested on a new dataset and the discrepancy was not being able to understand context while being trained. Understanding the context is the key in news identification, so the research turned to BERT, the Transformer model pre-trained with huge contextual data to perform this task. Drawing on its deep and diverse knowledge base, BERT has shown a remarkable aptitude for sorting news articles into fake/real categories based on their context. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and LSTM models demonstrated that although they were able to build models that were highly accurate up to 99% on familiar data, their accuracy dropped disproportionately as soon as new data was given. BERT, despite having a lower overall accuracy of 84% demonstrated a better sensitivity to contextual nuances in the news data. Here, the importance of contextualized conception in the sphere of fake news detection should be emphasized as a way to take advantage of BERT’s complicated comprehension which is a promising alternative of more accurate and effective identification as the media landscapes of the modern times may be complex and diverse. Despite the fact that the classical models surpass in planned environments, BERT’s capability of contextualization made it irreplaceable for evidence as the news sources in uncommon circumstances can digress from base.

articleTitle: Bank Note Authentication using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: The swift progression of technology has resulted in a surge in digital transactions, necessitating robust authentication mechanisms to avert fraudulent activities. Because genuine and counterfeit banknotes seem so identical, it is difficult, time-consuming, and error-prone for humans to determine which one is authentic. Counterfeit notes are manufactured at an alarmingly high rate, which means that systems for authenticating bank notes are essential to ensure counterfeit notes are detected and verified quickly and in due time. Such measures guarantee multiple benefits, including safe transactions, uphold the integrity of financial institutions, and guardianship against fake currency notes in the market. In this work, we show that automated solutions may be deployed to improve the accuracy and efficiency of procedures for banknote authentication. Currently, there is a lack of effective and precise models, which are especially trained for verifying or detecting bank note authentication, despite presence of an extensive research in the fields of artificial intelligence and machine learning. Our study seeks to close this gap by creating and implementing a deep learning model that can accurately identify and differentiate between real and fake banknotes. In the study, we noted that the suggested model outperformed conventional techniques with a notable degree of accuracy with the use of an extensive dataset. The model’s potential for practical implementation in banking and financial establishments is shown by its exceptional accuracy and efficiency in detecting fake banknotes. The high accuracy of the model demonstrates that deep learning may be used successfully to improve security protocols, opening the door for more developments in financial technology and otehr allied fields.

articleTitle: Securing the Pulse of Healthcare: A Survey of IoMT Security Challenges and AI-Powered Defenses
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: In this revolutionizing era of technology, the Internet of Things (IoT) has gained massive importance. One of its subsets is the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), providing a versatile platform where patients, practitioners, physicians, and other stakeholders can collaborate. This has enhanced the importance of technology in healthcare, assisted with artificial intelligence. Due to its emerging significance and synergy, IoMT is also susceptible to potential threats affecting branches such as medical devices, telemedicine, remote patient monitoring, and cloud healthcare infrastructure. This paper is primarily based on a thorough, critical, and comparative analysis that highlights certain potential vulnerabilities and their respective AI-based solutions. It is evident that AI is mitigating the risks and security threats affecting IoMT branches, but it is also opening new doors for adversaries to attack and compromise their security. This impact of AI can be eradicated or minimized with keen human intervention. Hence, the security of IoMT branches is highlighted in this paper along with their respective AI solutions, along with certain future recommendations to excel in this tech race.

articleTitle: The use of AR for the Development of Early Childhood Education: Little Learner App for Alphabets, Colors, and Poem learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: With the growth of information and technology and global integration, the popularity of early childhood education has become a hot topic that demands full concentration of a parent, tutor, child, and school. After reviewing the existing state of early childhood education, we found numerous issues, including challenges of grabbing attention of a kid in learning, difficulties of disabled children, lack of parental attention and old methods of teaching, and insufficient study effectiveness. Through the use of augmented reality (AR), this work suggests a novel method for learning poems, fundamental English alphabets, and color recognition for young children. Then, using augmented reality technology, we created a smartphone application named Little Learner for early children that teaches and assesses development around different ages. This application demonstrates exceptional effectiveness.

articleTitle: Intelligent Remote Sensing Vehicle Classification using YOLOv8 and Probabilistic Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Vehicle detection and classification represent critical tasks within intelligent traffic monitoring systems, yet traditional methods often pose computational challenges and limitations when adapting to varying data collection methods. This study provides a unique technique for vehicle recognition and classification in aerial image sequences. The suggested model involves six steps. Initially, all images undergo preprocessing to remove noise and boost brightness. At that point, foreground components are extracted using segmentation. Following segmentation, the YOLOv8 algorithm is used to identify vehicles. On the identified vehicles, feature extraction is then carried out using Learned Arrangements of Three Patch Codes (LATCH), Binary Robust Independent Elementary Features (BRIEF), and Accelerated-KAZE (AKAZE). Particle swarm optimization (PSO) was used to maximize the features. We classify via the Probabilistic Neural Network (PNN) classifier. Positive results are shown by experimental results on three datasets; on the AU-AIR dataset, the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 91%, and on the Roundabout dataset, 94%. Furthermore, a comparative analysis with other traditional approaches is provided to thoroughly evaluate the model’s performance.

articleTitle: Digital Board Pro: An Interactive Whiteboard
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Traditional whiteboards, while widely used in educational and professional settings around the world, suffer from limitations such as lack of interactivity, static content presentation, and the inability to save or manipulate information. Digital whiteboards and touchscreen systems, although offering advanced features, are often prohibitively expensive, require complex installations, and are highly sensitive and costly. To address these issues and revolutionize traditional whiteboards at a minimal cost, we propose a novel, real-time, interactive system that can be used on any surface, including walls, whiteboards, or even any kind of surface. Our system combines affordable components an infrared (IR) pen, a standard webcam, and a basic projector, along with advanced computer vision techniques. The proposed approach operates in three main stages: first, analyzing the webcam image to detect the IR pen; second, applying geometrical transformation theory to align the webcam view with the projected content; and third, translating the detected IR pen position into computer cursor movement, effectively turning any surface into an interactive display. The system achieves impressive results with a latency of only 0.033 seconds (30 fps) and 99% accuracy in editing at the exact desired point. Users can write, modify, edit, and draw directly on the projected content using the IR pen, offering a highly interactive and immersive experience. The practicality and versatility of the system have been demonstrated in various experiments, showcasing its potential to enhance interactive lectures, webinars, presentations, and educational interfaces, all at a fraction of the cost of conventional digital whiteboards.

articleTitle: Biases and Trustworthiness Challenges with Mitigation Strategies for Large Language Models in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Rapid innovations in Large Language Models (LLMs) have resulted in remarkably efficient decision-making and learning capacities, specifically in critical sectors such as healthcare. Domain-specific LLMs are progressively being designed for medical pre-screening and diagnostic procedures in healthcare. Despite these advancements, LLMs persist as opaque systems lacking the capacity to offer fair decisions and trustworthy explanations. Though various techniques are proposed to address challenges associated with LLMs, further research is considered essential to adopt LLMs in high-risk sectors. This article explores challenges related to LLMs along with suggested strategies for mitigation. Among several challenges, this study presents a comprehensive overview of biases and trustworthiness in healthcare LLMs. It presents an overview of clinical, cognitive, and demographic bias mitigation approaches at the Data, Model, and Inference levels. Further, it provides a detailed critical analysis of existing bias quantification metrics and healthcare benchmarks to assess trustworthiness in clinical LLMs. This research is supported by an empirical study, where existing patient records are extracted to fine-tune Llama2. The responses from fine-tuned Llama 2 are analyzed for various biases, and existing bias mitigation strategies are applied. However, the results indicate existing bias mitigation approaches need to be revised, highlighting the need for advanced techniques. This study concludes by explaining the essential research areas in bias mitigation and trustworthiness necessary to ensure the practical deployment of LLMs in clinical decision-making.

articleTitle: Current Development Status and Trend of Electric Vehicles in Pakistan: Policy Recommendations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
abstract: Pakistan has seen enormous growth in electric vehicles (EVs) and related development steps in recent years, in response to both environmental concerns and energy demands. This research first describes the current status of automobile infrastructure and its impact, current status of electric vehicle (EV) development in Pakistan, including infrastructure for charging, EV adoption challenges, EV policies summary and analysis, and policy recommendations. The development of EVs in Pakistan is then examined and analyzed, with a focus on government policies, financing for development, and rules pertaining to subsidies. In order to increase interest in the EV sector among academia, industry, and government, the study concludes by projecting the future development of EVs in Pakistan, taking into account industry, technological, and policy issues in addition to the opportunities and difficulties that lie ahead.
